data.title: Johnson & Johnson's prostate cancer drug shrinks tumors in early-stage trial
data.description:
Johnson & Johnson on Saturday said its experimental once-daily oral prostate cancer drug caused tumors to disappear or shrink in an early-stage trial.

J&J had gained access to the drug through its $3.05 billion deal to buy Halda Therapeutics last year.

Here are more details:

  • The company was testing JNJ-6143 in patients with advanced prostate cancer who had received multiple treatments

  • Its novel approach selectively kills cancer cells by interfering with a protein they need to survive

  • In the trial, 77% of 31 evaluable patients receiving the 50-milligram dose saw their PSA levels, a blood marker used to monitor prostate cancer, fall by at least 50%; in 48% of patients, PSA levels fell by at least 90%

  • Among patients whose tumors could be measured using imaging, 69% had a confirmed complete or partial response

  • "It adds a new mechanism of action to J&J's prostate cancer portfolio," a Johnson & Johnson spokesperson said

  • Common side effects were nausea and elevated cholesterol and triglyceride levels. One patient discontinued treatment due to adverse effects

  • The data were presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress

data.title: Compass Therapeutics Announces Publication of Phase 2/3 COMPANION-002 Results for Tovecimig in the Journal of Clinical Oncology and Oral Presentation at ESMO 2026
data.description:
Key points:
  • As published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology (JCO) and presented at ESMO, COMPANION-002 met its primary endpoint of ORR and key secondary endpoint of PFS, with a 56% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.
  • Responses were durable, with a median duration of response (DOR) of 4.9 months, and disease control rate (DCR) was also significantly improved (62.2% vs. 36.8%).
  • A new, post hoc analysis of overall survival (OS) included in the JCO publication uses the Two-Stage Estimation, an established method for adjusting for crossover, and demonstrates an OS hazard ratio of 0.85 (95% CI, 0.59–1.26; p=0.53).
  • Safety profile was consistent with prior tovecimig studies and the anti-VEGF class, with no new safety signals identified.

BOSTON, Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Compass Therapeutics, Inc. , a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary antibody-based therapeutics to treat multiple human diseases, today announced the publication of results from the positive Phase 2/3 COMPANION-002 study of tovecimig in combination with paclitaxel in patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC) in the Journal of Clinical Oncology (JCO). The results are also being presented today by Nilofer S. Azad, M.D., Johns Hopkins Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center, at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress in Madrid, Spain. The full publication is available via open access at https://ascopubs.org/toc/jco/0/ja.

COMPANION-002 is a randomized Phase 2/3 study that evaluated tovecimig plus paclitaxel versus paclitaxel alone in 168 patients with advanced BTC who had received one prior therapy. As previously reported, and now published following peer review, the study met its primary endpoint, with tovecimig plus paclitaxel demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in ORR of 18.0% vs. 5.3% with paclitaxel alone (p=0.0228) evaluated by blinded independent central review (BICR). The study also met its key secondary endpoint of PFS with a median PFS of 4.7 vs. 2.6 months (HR=0.44, p<0.0001), representing a 56% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.

Key findings from COMPANION-002 include:

  • Duration of response and disease control: Responses with tovecimig plus paclitaxel lasted a median of 4.9 months. The disease control rate, which includes patients whose cancer responded or remained stable, significantly improved at 62.2% vs. 36.8% with paclitaxel alone (p=0.0018).
  • Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma subgroup: Patients with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (cancer of the bile ducts inside the liver), a prespecified subgroup, made up more than half of the study population (92 of 168). In these patients, results were consistent with the overall study population, with an ORR of 15.3% vs. 0% (p=0.0258) and median PFS of 5.1 vs. 3.0 months (HR=0.32).
  • Overall survival (OS) and crossover-adjusted analysis: Patients in the paclitaxel arm could cross over to tovecimig plus paclitaxel arm after BICR-confirmed progression. 31 of 57 (54%) patients crossed over, resulting in 85% of all patients in the study (142 of 168) ultimately receiving tovecimig. The intent-to-treat OS analysis was confounded by the high rate of crossover and no statistically significant difference in OS was observed. To estimate the treatment effect if crossover had not occurred, the JCO publication includes a post hoc exploratory analysis using the Two-Stage Estimation, an established method for adjusting for crossover, in which the OS hazard ratio was 0.85 (95% CI, 0.59–1.26; p=0.53).
  • Outcomes in crossover patients: Among the 31 patients who crossed over, median PFS after the addition of tovecimig to paclitaxel, a prespecified secondary endpoint, was 3.5 months, compared with 1.9 months during their initial treatment with paclitaxel alone (HR=0.40, p=0.0035). In a post hoc exploratory analysis, these patients who crossed over to receive tovecimig had a median OS of 12.8 months, compared with 6.1 months for control-arm patients who did not cross over (HR=0.54, p=0.04), even though crossover patients had progressed more quickly on initial paclitaxel treatment. These crossover comparisons were not randomized and are exploratory.
  • Safety: The safety profile was generally manageable and consistent with prior tovecimig studies and the anti-VEGF class, with no new safety signals identified. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) in the combination arm were hypertension (69%) and fatigue (67%). Grade 3 or higher TEAEs occurred in 93.5% of patients in the combination arm and 64.2% of patients who received paclitaxel alone. TEAEs leading to overall treatment discontinuation occurred in 27.8% and 11.3%, respectively, and were mostly consistent with known anti-angiogenic and chemotherapy toxicities. No hypertensive crises or unexpected severe cardiovascular toxicities were observed. TEAEs leading to death occurred in 5.6% and 1.9% of patients, respectively.

“COMPANION-002 is an important, randomized study in patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer,” said Dr. Azad. “The significant improvements in response rate and progression-free survival, together with the durability of responses and disease control, are encouraging for patients in this setting. We also saw activity in patients who switched to tovecimig after their disease progressed on paclitaxel alone, which is notable in a setting where disease often progresses quickly.”

"Publication of the COMPANION-002 results in the Journal of Clinical Oncology following independent peer review is a significant milestone for patients with BTC," said Thomas Schuetz, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Compass. "These data, including the new two-stage estimation adjusting for the crossover impact on overall survival, strengthen our conviction that tovecimig has the potential to make a meaningful difference for patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer who have few treatment options. We are determined to bring tovecimig to these patients and will continue working with the FDA toward that goal."

Additional analyses from COMPANION-002, including patient-reported quality of life and translational research, are ongoing and will be reported separately.

About Tovecimig

Tovecimig is an investigational DLL4 x VEGF-A bispecific antibody designed to block two angiogenic pathways simultaneously, representing a first-in-class approach to disrupting tumor angiogenesis. In COMPANION-002, tovecimig was evaluated in combination with paclitaxel in patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer. Tovecimig has received Fast Track and Orphan Drug Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Tovecimig remains investigational and has not been approved by the FDA.

About Biliary Tract Cancer

BTC is an aggressive, life-threatening cancer estimated to affect approximately 26,500 patients annually in the United States. For the vast majority of patients with BTC whose tumors do not harbor an actionable mutation with an approved targeted therapy, there is currently no FDA-approved treatment in the second-line setting. The therapies most commonly used in this setting, which are not labeled or approved by the FDA for the treatment of patients with BTC, generally have an ORR of approximately 5% or less.

About COMPANION-002

COMPANION-002 (NCT05506943) is a randomized, controlled Phase 2/3 study of tovecimig in patients with unresectable advanced, metastatic or recurrent BTC who received one prior systemic chemotherapy regimen. The study randomized 168 patients 2:1 to tovecimig plus paclitaxel (n=111) or paclitaxel alone (n=57). The primary endpoint was ORR by blinded independent central review; secondary endpoints included PFS, OS and duration of response.

About Compass Therapeutics

Compass Therapeutics is a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the standard of care for patients with cancer through the discovery and development of innovative antibody-based therapeutics. The company leverages deep expertise in tumor biology and proprietary antibody engineering technologies to develop differentiated therapies that target the intersection of angiogenesis, immune activation, and tumor-driven immunosuppression. Compass has a robust pipeline of novel product candidates in clinical development designed to address significant unmet needs and improve outcomes for patients with cancer. data.title: Celcuity Presents Updated Results from the PIK3CA MT Cohort of the Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 Study in Patients with HR+/HER2- Advanced Breast Cancer at the ESMO Congress 2026
data.description:
Median PFS was 21.5 months with the gedatolisib triplet and 11.5 months with the gedatolisib doublet versus 9.1 months with alpelisib + fulvestrant in patients who had no liver metastases

ORR and median duration of response was 59% and 19.4 months for the gedatolisib triplet and 43% and 27.8 months for the gedatolisib doublet, respectively, compared to 33% and 7.5 months for alpelisib + fulvestrant

The discontinuation rate for gedatolisib due to treatment-emergent adverse events was 5% and 4% with the gedatolisib triplet and doublet, respectively, compared to 19% for alpelisib

MINNEAPOLIS, Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Celcuity Inc. , a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing targeted therapies for the treatment of multiple solid tumor indications, today announced new subgroup analyses from the PIK3CA mutant (“MT”) cohort of the Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 study evaluating gedatolisib in patients with HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (“ABC”). These data were presented by Dr. Barbara Pistilli, Head of the Breast Cancer Unit, Gustave Roussy, at the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 today, Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 4:15 a.m. EST/10:15 a.m. CEST during a late breaking rapid oral presentation:

Presentation LBA 16: VIKTORIA-1: Updated results of a randomized, open-label, phase 3 study of gedatolisib (geda) + fulvestrant (fulv) ± palbociclib (palbo) vs standard of care in patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer (ABC) (Study 2)

In the PIK3CA mutant cohort, the discontinuation rate of gedatolisib due to treatment-emergent adverse events (“TEAEs”) was 5% and 4% for the gedatolisib triplet and doublet, respectively, compared to a 19% discontinuation rate due to TEAEs for alpelisib. Grade 3 stomatitis with gedatolisib was transient. By the second cycle of treatment, less than 3% of patients had Grade 3 stomatitis, and all grade 3 events improved within 1-2 weeks. Discontinuations due to stomatitis for the gedatolisib triplet and gedatolisib doublet were minimal, 1% and 0%, respectively.

“The additional data from Study 2 of VIKTORIA-1 show consistent and significant clinical benefit for important sub-groups of breast cancer patients treated with gedatolisib regimens,” said Igor Gorbachevsky, Chief Medical Officer of Celcuity. “For patients who do not have liver metastases and received the gedatolisib triplet, the median progression-free survival was approximately 21 months, versus approximately 9 months for the alpelisib regimen. This is a particularly important result since patients with no liver metastases represent approximately 60%-70% of all patients treated in this setting.”

“Additionally, the median duration of response was over 19 months for the gedatolisib triplet in both the PIK3CA wild-type cohort, or Study 1, and the PIK3CA mutant cohort, or Study 2, compared to not evaluable for fulvestrant in the PIK3CA wild-type cohort and 7.5 months for alpelisib plus fulvestrant in the PIK3CA mutant cohort. To our knowledge, the gedatolisib triplet in each study demonstrated the longest median duration of response results ever reported for a therapeutic regimen used in the primary analysis for a Phase 3 trial in the second-line HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer setting.”

VIKTORIA-1 PIK3CA Wild-Type Cohort Comparative Analysis

Dr. Sara Tolaney, Chief of the Division of Breast Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, presented a comparative analysis of data for the gedatolisib regimens from the PIK3CA wild-type cohort of VIKTORIA-1 and other regimens evaluated in patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer.

Poster 1873P: Gedatolisib (Ged) vs Other Regimens Post-CDK4/6i and Endocrine Therapy (ET) in PIK3CA Wild-Type (WT) HR+/ HER2- Advanced Breast Cancer (aBC): A Network Meta-Analysis (NMA)

Eight studies were included in this network meta-analysis comparing progression-free survival outcomes in randomized controlled trials of systemic treatments evaluated among patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer with CDK4/6 inhibitor experience and PIK3CA wild-type tumors. This analysis found that the gedatolisib triplet and doublet each demonstrated statistically significant or numerically superior improvement in PFS and in progression-free survival rate at 6 months relative to the non-gedatolisib regimens evaluated. Of note, the analysis found that patients treated with the gedatolisib triplet and doublet were a statistically significant 2x and 1.5x more likely to survive without disease progression or death compared to imlunestrant plus abemaciclib, respectively.

About HR+/HER2- Breast Cancer

Breast cancer is the second most common cancer and one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide.1 More than two million breast cancer cases were diagnosed globally in 2022.1 While survival rates are high for those diagnosed with early breast cancer, only approximately 30% of patients who are diagnosed with or who progress to metastatic disease are expected to live five years after their diagnosis.2 HR+/HER2- breast cancer is the most common subtype of breast cancer, accounting for approximately 70% of all breast cancers.2

About Celcuity

Celcuity is a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing targeted therapies for the treatment of multiple solid tumor indications. The company's first FDA-approved product is REVTORPYK™ (gedatolisib), pan-PI3K and mTORC1/2 inhibitor that comprehensively blockades the PAM (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway. Its mechanism of action and pharmacokinetic properties are differentiated from other currently approved and investigational therapies that target PI3Kα, AKT or mTORC1 alone or together. A Phase 3 clinical trial, VIKTORIA-1, evaluating gedatolisib in combination with fulvestrant with or without palbociclib in patients with HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, supported FDA approval of REVTORPYK for use in patients without a PIK3CA mutation detected following progression on or after treatment with at least one line of endocrine therapy in the metastatic setting. Results for the PIK3CA mutant cohort of VIKTORIA-1 have been released. VIKTORIA-2 is an ongoing Phase 3 clinical trial incorporating two independent studies, Study 1 and Study 2, in two separate cohorts of patients with ABC who are treatment-naive in the advanced setting. Study 1 is evaluating gedatolisib plus palbociclib plus fulvestrant as first-line treatment for patients with endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2- ABC. Study 2 is evaluating gedatolisib plus palbociclib plus letrozole as first-line treatment for patients with endocrine-sensitive HR+/HER2- ABC. A Phase 1/2 clinical trial, CELC-G-201, evaluating gedatolisib in combination with darolutamide in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, is ongoing. More detailed information about Celcuity’s active clinical trials can be found at ClinicalTrials.gov. Celcuity is headquartered in Minneapolis. Further information about Celcuity can be found at www.celcuity.com. Follow us on LinkedIn and X.

data.title: Bitdeer Reports 1,355 Bitcoin Mined In September While Building AI Capacity
data.description:
TL;DR: Bitdeer says its September Bitcoin production reached 1,355 BTC, highlighting the miner’s expanding hash rate alongside separate data-center and AI-service plans.

Bitdeer has released another sizable set of Bitcoin mining numbers as the industry weighs how much computing infrastructure should remain dedicated to hashing and how much can be redirected toward artificial intelligence services.

In its latest monthly operating update, published October 19, the company reported mining 1,355 BTC in September. It put the comparable figure a year earlier at 452 BTC, making the latest result roughly three times that level. The performance illustrates the consequences of adding mining capacity, though it does not by itself establish whether returns improved after power and equipment costs.

Hash rate is not profit

The company's report provides figures for its different computing operations, including a self-mining hash rate of 82.3 EH/s and co-mining capacity of 28.7 EH/s. Those categories refer to different arrangements and should not be combined carelessly into a single profit forecast.

A miner's monthly Bitcoin production reflects not only its hardware but also global network conditions. Difficulty adjustments, transaction fees, power availability and equipment efficiency change the number of coins that a given fleet can earn.

Even rising production can be accompanied by financial pressure if more competitors install machines or if the average cost of electricity rises. Investors should pair BTC output data with capital expenditure, cash costs and reported profitability before treating mined coins as free cash flow.

The separate opportunity in AI data centers

Bitdeer also describes an expanding pipeline for AI cloud and infrastructure services. The update references capacity agreements in Malaysia, with planned delivery windows extending into 2027 and 2028.

Those projects operate on a different commercial clock from a new Bitcoin miner brought online this month. A data-center agreement can represent future contracted capacity without proving that the site is finished, fully occupied or generating its forecast revenue today.

The convergence narrative has become popular among large miners because both industries need electricity, facilities and cooling. But the workloads use different processing hardware, and converting a mining site into AI infrastructure can require substantial additional investment.

Bitdeer's production update offers a useful snapshot of a company pursuing both routes. The near-term Bitcoin figures are realized operational results; the AI figures include plans and contracted capacity dependent on delivery.

That distinction will matter as analysts assess whether the company can sustain cash-generating mining operations while funding what may become a much larger infrastructure business over time.

data.title: BeOne Presents Compelling Data in Hard-to-Treat Liver and Lung Cancers at ESMO 2026
data.description:
BeOne Medicines Ltd. (; HKEX: 06160; ), a global oncology company, today announced new data from multiple differentiated investigational medicines across its priority solid tumor disease areas at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 (October 23–27, Madrid). The presentations span gastrointestinal, lung, and breast cancers, and reflect the growing momentum of BeOne’s solid tumor franchise.

Mark Lanasa, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer, Solid Tumors at BeOne, said:

“At ESMO, we are showing how our strategy of matching the right modality to disease biology is translating into meaningful clinical progress. Our GPC3 x 4-1BB bispecific antibody continues to be well tolerated and demonstrates durable activity with longer follow up in patients with heavily pre-treated hepatocellular carcinoma, while the first clinical data from our brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor and CEA-targeting ADC expand our innovation in non-small cell lung cancer. Alongside the global Phase 3 KANDELA-302 study of our CDK4 inhibitor in breast cancer, these advances mark a clear step forward as BeOne’s solid tumor pipeline moves from promising science toward medicines with the potential to improve outcomes in difficult-to-treat cancers.”

Potential first-in-class GPC3×4-1BB bispecific continues to demonstrate compelling and durable activity in heavily pretreated HCC (Proffered Paper: 1679O; October 24, 10:15–11:45 CET)

Patients with advanced HCC who progress after immunotherapy face a high unmet need, with no established standard of care and five-year survival of only approximately 20%1,2. BGB-B2033 is an investigational bispecific antibody designed to address this gap by activating 4-1BB on T cells in the presence of GPC3-expressing tumor cells, concentrating immune activation at the tumor site, and limiting systemic toxicity, a key consideration for HCC patients who frequently suffer from underlying liver disease.

Updated Phase 1 results include the first disclosure of dose-optimization data and longer follow-up from dose escalation. Among 94 patients, 93.6% had received prior PD-(L)1 therapy and 61.7% had received both PD-(L)1 therapy and a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Highlights include:

  • At the recommended Phase 3 dose of 450 mg every three weeks, the confirmed objective response rate (ORR) was 36.0%, a result that exceeds efficacy observed with TKIs, which have shown an ORR of approximately 5% in late-line HCC.3

  • At the selected Phase 3 dose, the estimated six-month confirmed duration-of-response rate was 74.1%, with responses observed across all clinically relevant patient subgroups.

  • Across dose levels, Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 5.3% of patients, and treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation in only 2.1%.

BGB-B2033 received Fast Track Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in December 2025, as well as Orphan Drug Designation from the FDA in March 2026 and the European Commission in October 2026 for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). BeOne plans to initiate global registrational clinical trials in late-line HCC by the end of 2026, while also developing plans for registrational studies in earlier treatment settings.

Initial first-in-human data from two differentiated assets advance BeOne’s emerging NSCLC portfolio

At ESMO 2026, BeOne is presenting initial clinical data in NSCLC from two biomarker-led programs with distinct mechanisms: the oral, brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor, BGB-58067, and the CEA-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), BG-C477. Based on these promising data, both programs are intended to advance toward late-stage development in 2027, continuing to build BeOne’s footprint in lung cancer alongside its established program with TEVIMBRA (tislelizumab).

Brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor, BGB-58067, demonstrates systemic and intracranial activity in MTAP-deficient NSCLC (Poster: 1043P; October 23, 3:15–4:00 PM CET)

BGB-58067 is a highly potent, brain-penetrant methylthioadenosine (MTA)-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor designed to exploit the vulnerability created by MTAP deficiency. In this, the largest publicly shared data set in MTAP-deficient solid tumors, initial Phase 1 findings from 182 patients, including 83 with NSCLC, showed:

  • Among 75 efficacy-evaluable patients with MTAP-deficient NSCLC, confirmed ORR was 25.3% and disease control rate (DCR) was 76.0%. In the EGFR wild-type subgroup, confirmed ORR was 38.5% and DCR was 82.1%.

  • Median progression-free survival was 7.7 months in the overall NSCLC cohort and 8.1 months in the EGFR wild-type subgroup.

  • In the NSCLC cohort, an intracranial objective response rate of 30.8% was observed in patients with untreated, asymptomatic brain metastases as well as a low rate of central nervous system (CNS) progression in 2L+ NSCLC.

  • At daily doses of 200–400 mg (n=87), Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27.6%, and treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation in 5.7%. The most common treatment-related events were nausea, anemia and fatigue.

CEA-targeting ADC BG-C477 achieves encouraging response rate in previously-treated CEAhigh NSCLC (Poster: 2567P; October 26, 12:00–12:45 PM CET)

BG-C477 is the first ADC to emerge from BeOne’s internal drug discovery organization. With a proprietary CEA (or CEACAM5) targeting antibody, a highly stable conjugator, and a cleavable linker, BG-C477 is designed to deliver a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor payload directly to CEA-expressing tumor cells.

As of April 9, 2026, preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy findings from 43 heavily pretreated patients with NSCLC, including 25 with high CEA expression, showed:

  • Confirmed ORR was 56.0% in patients with CEAhigh NSCLC, with a disease control rate of 88.0%; confirmed ORR in the overall NSCLC population was 34.9%.

  • Among patients with CEAhigh NSCLC, median duration of response had not been reached. The majority of responders, as well as two patients with unconfirmed responses, remained on treatment at data cutoff.

  • Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were predominantly hematologic events (anemia 14.0%, neutropenia 14.0%, thrombocytopenia 2.3%).

Updated results, with a more recent data cut-off, will be presented in the Locally Advanced NSCLC poster session on Monday, October 26 at 12:00 CET. BG-C477 received Fast Track Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in October 2026.

Pivotal-study update: Phase 3 KANDELA-302 trial of CDK4 inhibitor BGB-43395 now enrolling in first-line HR+/HER2-negative breast cancer (1885TiP; October 24, 12:00–12:45 PM CEST)

Building on previously reported Phase 1 activity and tolerability findings, BeOne is advancing BGB-43395, an investigational selective CDK4 inhibitor, in the global Phase 3 KANDELA-302 study (NCT07492641). The study compares BGB-43395 plus letrozole with investigator’s choice of abemaciclib, palbociclib or ribociclib plus letrozole in first-line HR+/HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

Enrollment began in May 2026, with patients planned across North and South America, Europe, Asia and Australia. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, with overall survival as the key secondary endpoint.

About BGB-B2033
BGB-B2033 is a bispecific antibody targeting GPC3 (glypican 3), a tumor-specific antigen highly expressed in HCC4, and 4-1BB, a co-stimulatory receptor associated with T-cell activation and tumor reactivity in HCC.5 The molecule has been designed with reduced antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) to prevent systemic toxicity.

About BGB-58067
BGB-58067 is an investigational, oral small molecule designed to inhibit protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) in an MTA-dependent manner, enabling selective targeting of MTAP-deleted cancer cells. Preclinical data demonstrate enhanced selectivity compared with MTAP wild-type cells, as well as strong potency and brain penetration.

About BG-C477
BG-C477 is an investigational ADC designed to target CEA, also known as CEACAM5, a protein highly expressed in several epithelial cancers, including certain lung and gastrointestinal cancers. The molecule is designed to work as a targeted delivery system, using an antibody that specifically recognizes CEA to deliver a potent anti-cancer payload to CEA-expressing tumor cells. BG-C477 incorporates a highly stable conjugator and cleavable linker, aiming for a strong bystander effect and manageable toxicity.

About BGB-43395
BGB-43395 is an investigational cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4 inhibitor being studied in a global clinical development program that includes the KANDELA-302 (NCT07492641) Phase 3 clinical trial, in hormone receptor-positive (HR+)/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) breast cancer. BGB-43395 is a highly potent and selective CDK4 inhibitor that may reduce dose-limiting hematologic toxicities associated with the current CDK4/6 standard of care and improve tolerability, thereby enabling deeper CDK4 inhibition.

About BeOne
BeOne Medicines is a global oncology company that is discovering and developing innovative treatments for cancer patients worldwide. With a portfolio spanning hematology and solid tumors, BeOne is expediting development of its diverse pipeline of novel therapeutics through its internal capabilities and collaborations. The Company has a growing global team spanning six continents who are driven by scientific excellence and exceptional speed to reach more patients than ever before. To learn more about BeOne, please visit www.beonemedicines.com and follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

data.title: Demeter's Ashwini Agarwal sees value in largecaps, financial services and consumer stocks; avoids IT and OMCs
data.description:
Ashwini Agarwal, Founder and Partner at Demeter Advisors, believes large-cap stocks offer better return potential than midcaps and smallcaps over the next 12 months, following the recent correction in Indian equity markets.

He sees opportunities in financial services, consumer staples, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and select manufacturing companies, where stock prices have fallen despite businesses continuing to perform.

The recent sell-off has widened the valuation gap between largecap and smallcap stocks, making the former more attractive relative to their earnings growth, Agarwal said.

He added, “On a bottom-up basis, there are still opportunities in the wider market. But on a top-down basis, the chances that you make money on largecaps over the next 12 months are far higher than you will make money in smallcaps at an index level that's how I think about it. So opportunities exist, but on a top-down basis, largecaps look far more attractive.”

According to Agarwal, the Nifty has delivered annualised returns of around 5% since December 2022, while earnings have grown by about 8% annually. In contrast, the Nifty 250 smallcap index has risen by around 9% annually, against earnings growth of approximately 6%. This suggests that largecap valuations have declined while smallcap valuations have expanded over the same period.

Agarwal believes the correction has created opportunities for long-term investors, particularly in stocks where earnings have improved but valuations have fallen.

However, he cautioned that uncertainty around global energy and transportation costs, along with fluctuations in raw material prices, could affect corporate earnings.

"Staples are giving an entry opportunity," Agarwal said, pointing to opportunities in consumer staples and tobacco stocks. He believes some of these companies have seen significant corrections, even as their businesses continue to offer value. Strong dividend yields could also provide support to investors in select stocks.

Financial services is another area he favours. Agarwal said earnings in the sector have improved over the past six months, but share prices have not reflected the improvement. Credit quality remains healthy, spreads are stable and liquidity conditions, although tighter recently, remain manageable.

Within financial services, he favours select private-sector banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). He also sees potential in microfinance stocks, where valuations have fallen substantially over the past three to four years. Some companies are trading below their book value, although he acknowledged that drought-related stress could affect parts of the sector.

He also sees opportunities in offline retail, particularly clothing, where valuations have fallen sharply. While the shift towards online shopping has affected the sector, he believes the decline in stock prices has been more severe than the underlying business performance warrants.

Select chemical and pharmaceutical companies have also become attractive following recent corrections. Agarwal believes investors should take a longer-term view of these sectors rather than focus only on near-term concerns around input costs and earnings.

Agarwal remains positive on Indian exporters, including apparel and engineering companies, as well as businesses in chemicals and contract development and manufacturing. He believes expanding export markets and the ability of Indian companies to meet specialised customer requirements could support growth over the next three years.

He is also comfortable holding hospital stocks despite concerns around regulatory intervention and possible price caps. Agarwal argued that hospitals need sustainable returns to attract investment and expand capacity, particularly given India's shortage of hospital infrastructure.

On information technology services, however, he remains cautious. He said the impact of artificial intelligence on the sector's business model is still unclear, making it difficult to assess the industry's long-term earnings outlook.

Agarwal added policy uncertainty remains a key concern for investors in oil marketing companies (OMCs) and gas companies. He noted that oil companies do not have complete freedom to set petrol and diesel prices, which creates uncertainty around their earnings despite fluctuations in crude oil prices.

Agarwal said frequent policy changes across sectors, including hospitals, insurance distribution and brokerage services, have made investors cautious. He stressed the need for a stable policy framework over the next five years, adding that sudden regulatory changes could affect companies' earnings and investment decisions.

Passengers should check their flight status with IndiGo before travelling to the airport.

Akasa Air has extended flight suspensions to and from Jeddah until November 10 and Riyadh until November 30, 2026.

In a travel update on October 23, the airline said: "In view of the prevailing security situation in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and following a careful assessment of the safety environment, Akasa Air has extended the suspension of flights to and from the following destinations: Jeddah: Until and including November 10, 2026; Riyadh: Until and including November 30, 2026."

The airline said it was monitoring developments in real time. Affected passengers can opt for a full refund, credited to the original payment method within seven days, or reschedule without an additional charge. Those who booked through travel partners should contact them directly.

"The safety and well-being of our passengers and crew remain our highest priority," Akasa Air said.

Air India and Air India Express have suspended flights to and from Jeddah, Riyadh and Dammam through October 24, 2026, according to the reported travel updates.

The suspensions follow attacks on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield on October 21. The MEA said an Indian national was killed and two others were injured in the Dammam incident, while another Indian citizen was injured at the oilfield.

Saudi Arabia is home to approximately 2.74 million Indian nationals. The Indian Embassy has urged them to remain alert, follow instructions from Saudi authorities and move to a safe place inside a building during an aerial attack. It has also warned against filming or sharing images of interceptions and impact sites, citing possible legal consequences under Saudi law.

MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said approximately 3,000 stranded Umrah pilgrims had returned to India over the previous week, while more than 10,000 other pilgrims had travelled home on available flights.

The Indian Embassy in Riyadh and Consulate General in Jeddah are coordinating with airlines and tour operators to help remaining affected pilgrims return. The missions are also providing welfare assistance, operating 24-hour control rooms and issuing regular advisories.

The Indian mission has said nationals requiring urgent departure may consider transiting through Bahrain, Kuwait or Qatar, subject to obtaining the necessary visas.

data.title: Data recap: FPI selloff, Reliance bets, Blinkit's expansion plans
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- From foreign investors continuing to pull money out of Indian equities to unusual leveraged bets on Reliance Industries Ltd, the week saw key developments across markets and business.

Eternal raised its target for Blinkit's dark store expansion, while the government outlined plans to corporatize 11 major ports to speed up decision-making. Meanwhile, Australian pacer Mitchell Starc reached the 450-wicket milestone in men's Test cricket, joining an elite group of bowlers-here is this week's news in numbers.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) pulled out Rs.48,056 crore from Indian equities till 23 October, extending the exodus of foreign capital from the market. High crude oil prices, rising US bond yields and a stronger dollar have weighed on investor sentiment.

If October ends with net outflows, it will be the seventh month in 2026 to see foreign investors pull money out of Indian equities. Cumulative net outflows have reached about Rs.3.10 trillion this year, nearly double the Rs.1.66 trillion recorded in 2025.

Last week, finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman flagged the flight of foreign capital towards the US and markets offering greater opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI) as 'a concern'.

Two traders have built large leveraged positions in Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), a move analysts have described as 'rarest of rare', a Mint report said. Stock exchange data shows that both traders hold positions exceeding 3% each of RIL's marketwide position limit (MWPL).

The unusual bets come ahead of the initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms Ltd, RIL's telecom and digital services subsidiary, in which it owns about 66%. They also come as RIL shares have fallen sharply, hitting a 52-week low on 13 October.

India's most-valued listed company, RIL, could see value unlocked through Jio Platforms' public listing, which would give the subsidiary an independent market valuation. However, the rationale behind the traders' bets remains unclear.

Eternal is stepping up its expansion plans for quick-commerce business Blinkit, raising its target to 3,500 dark stores by March 2027 from the earlier target of 3,000. The company had 2,751 stores as of September 2026, adding 308 during the second quarter.

Eternal's consolidated revenue from operations rose 77.6% year-on-year to Rs.24,138 crore in the September quarter. However, profit margins remained thin, and the company reported a cash outflow of Rs.1,813 crore. Blinkit accounted for 80% of Eternal's revenue, making its expansion central to the company's growth plans.

Eternal remains confident that opening more stores in smaller cities will make business sense. The higher store target also comes as its main rival, Zepto, faces hurdles in raising funds.

7.9%: This is the year-on-year growth in India's core sector output in September, up from 5.9% in August. Iron ore, electricity, coal and refinery products led the growth.

759: Number of H-1B visa registrations filed by Infosys for FY27, down from 8,886 a year earlier, amid tighter US immigration policies. TCS registrations fell to 284 from 5,955 last year.

6.5%: Decline in vehicle registrations during this year's Navratri festival, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (Fada). The 2025 festival period had also benefited from GST cuts.

15: Amazon delivery facilities in New York that the e-commerce giant has threatened to close if a proposed bill mandating direct employment of delivery drivers becomes law.

28%: Share of software budgets that large enterprises spend, on average, on vendor upgrades and licensing, leaving less room for investment in AI and innovation, according to a study by software maintenance provider Origina.

The government plans to convert 11 of India's 12 major ports into professionally managed companies with independent boards by 2030. The move aims to speed up decisions on port operations, funding and expansion. Under the current system, administrative processes can slow decisions when cargo patterns change or customers' needs evolve.

Over the past four years, the combined revenue of the 12 major ports has grown at a compounded annual rate of 10.7%. Kamarajar Port near Chennai is the only major port currently run as a company. Under the proposed model, the port company will manage basic infrastructure, while private operators will run terminals and handle cargo under public-private partnership agreements. The new structure is expected to help ports respond more quickly to business needs and facilitate expansion.

Mitchell Starc's 450th Test wicket this week put him among an elite group of 10 bowlers to reach the milestone. The Australian left-arm pacer dismissed South Africa's Wiaan Mulder in the second Test, reaching the landmark in his 109th match. Sri Lankan spinner Muttiah Muralitharan leads the list with 800 wickets in 133 Tests.

However, Starc stands apart for his strike rate, that is, the speed at which he takes wickets. He needs just 46 balls, on average, to claim a wicket-the lowest among the 10 bowlers in the list. That makes him the quickest wicket-taker in the group, though not the most economical. Starc concedes 3.43 runs per over, reflecting the trade-off that comes with his attacking style: he takes wickets quickly but also gives batters more scoring opportunities.

data.title: Yoska CEO Deepak Raj: The man who brought Hyrox and Ironman to India
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Inside Hall 6 of the Nesco exhibition centre in Mumbai, the corridor throbs with activity on a mid-September weekend. Hundreds of annoyingly fit-looking people, most in fitted T-shirts, some men shirtless, walk around purposefully. Some pose in front of Hyrox signboards, flexing their muscles, grinning with accomplishment as their participation is registered for posterity.

Past the buzz of people in the hallway, past a door and inside the 15,000 square metre main hall, where the fitness event is underway, pumping music blares on speakers as participants run around in circles. A bridge takes spectators over the runners and to a central atrium where several others sit on rowing machines, push weights, pull weights, grimace, sweat, and impossibly, laugh.

Outside, in a lounge area of sorts, Deepak Raj, 49, looks reasonably composed. The chief executive officer and chief coach of Yoska, a Bengaluru-based integrated digital platform for endurance fitness that has a joint venture with German-headquartered fitness race brand Hyrox, is used to holding events of this scale and therefore, immune to the sensory overload.

Hyrox combines eight cycles of 1km runs interspersed with functional movements, including sled push, sled pull, burpee box broad jumps and farmers carry. In less than a decade since it started in Hamburg, the sport-fitness module has become a global rage, picking up especially rapidly in India. In a little over a year, since May 2025, six events have been held, in Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru. Coming up are editions in Gandhinagar in November, Noida in January 2027 and Bengaluru next May.

Seated on a bench, dressed in athleisure, Raj narrates the story of how he came to be associated with Hyrox. Just 48 hours after he first heard of it some years ago, intrigued and interested, he sent a cold email to a bunch of addresses mentioned on the website. are ones you don't expect replies from and he didn't either.

The opening line of his text apologised for writing to three-four email addresses, but his pitch claimed that India was primed for, not just Hyrox, but fitness, to grow the community and to work with global franchises. He was pleasantly surprised, therefore, to get a reply in two days. Within a few months, he was speaking to the CEO Christian Toetzke. By late 2024, the joint venture had materialised and Raj had added another property to his inventory.

In 2019, Yoska had brought Ironman 70.3 to India, its first edition and subsequent ones run in Goa-barring the two pandemic years. Unlike Hyrox, the triathlon was more personal for Raj, who had competed in a few and had worked towards getting it to India. "My goal was always to create enough platforms and avenues for people to either take up a healthy habit, lifestyle, fitness or sustain what they have started," he says. "To give them enough motivation and purpose, milestones, goals and races to do it."

Having a conversation with Raj in this high-adrenalin setting comes with its challenges, especially since we are seated on a communal bench in a common area. Groups of people join in occasionally to share the bench, but sportingly move along when requested.

Growing up in Bengaluru, Raj was good enough to get into St Joseph's High School's B team for basketball, a sport that he continues to favour. The reason he couldn't get into the A team, he reckons and backed by a school coach's assessment, was that he, ironically, didn't have the stamina.

Engineering followed at Bangalore University's Ambedkar College, and then a job at Infosys starting as a developer in 2000. The job sent him on a project with Adidas to Germany, among other places, where Raj saw people twice his age cycling to work. At Herzogenaurach, the town where Adidas is headquartered, an "overweight" Raj changed his life.

Running progressively long distances, he signed up for the Berlin marathon, completing it in under 5 hours. It took a few years before he did a sub-4 hours, tried a few small triathlons, but unconvincingly because he was not confident in the water. A posting in Brisbane from 2008, surrounded by outdoorsy Australians, gave him the confidence to embrace open water more boldly. He first heard of Ironman (3.8km swim, 180km bike, 42.2km run) on ESPN, and on 6 April 2008, a date he clearly remembers, Raj competed in his first half-distance Ironman (70.3; with 1.9km swim, 90km bike, 21.1km run).

"I had to get over the fear but I'm still slightly afraid of open water. I've done a lot of Ironman, but that doesn't mean my fear has gone," says Raj who now shuttles between Bengaluru and Australia, where his wife and son live.

"I sort of compartmentalised, parked that fear because there's lots of people around, you get strength in numbers."

By 2012, he was trying to break the 11-hour barrier for the Ironman, travelling and spending time away from family when he could feel his body breaking down. He considered a lifestyle change, discussed becoming a coach for endurance events with wife Hema.

He gave himself six months. In 2013, he formed a company, Tri a New Life (later Yoska as a digital platform), and started coaching people for free, then for a fee. He started doing camps and clinics while working on bringing Ironman to India.

Six years, three months and 20 days later, on 20 October 2019, India held its first Ironman 70.3.

Raj thought such a big property would entice sponsors to put in "crores, but got just Rs.21 lakh in sponsorship".

The process was arduous-convincing US-headquartered Ironman, an operator of participation sports, that India is ready, convincing the Goa state government to close down Panjim-Miramar roads for 12 hours on a Sunday, getting permissions, managing safety, and building a team while playing multiple roles, including race director.

Dark times followed during the subsequent pandemic years, but by 2022, Rs.3-4 crore could be raised in sponsorships. Later years were better with angel investors coming in to Yoska-many of them long-distance runners or triathletes coached by Raj who were also heads of successful companies. Sahil Barua, co-founder of logistics company Delhivery, Yashish Dahiya of insurance aggregator Policy Bazaar, Raghunandan G, founder of car rental aggregator TaxiForSure, besides venture capital firm Rainmatter in 2024-added to the cumulative investment purse of Rs.8.48 crore.

It was in September 2023, when Raj had just come back from Ironman Worlds in France that he got invited to a Hyrox-styled training session with a friend. He took 48 hours to understand the sport before sending that email.

After getting connected to Toetzke, Raj didn't wait for him to come to India for a recce; instead, he flew to Austria on a "very expensive last-minute flight" for the Vienna Hyrox. Toetzke followed up with a visit to India, where he was taken to all potential Hyrox facilities, including Nesco, which then was "a hole in the ground with two pillars".

The reason for Hyrox's growing popularity is, Raj explains, that while runners had marathons and other running events, there was no competitive or community event for the category of people colloquially called "gym bros". Besides, Hyrox's singularity is in its packaging-collating existing exercises, like sandbag lunges, with runs to create a uniform system that's the same across the world. Timings could be compared across events, and athletes could aim to improve their performances through timings.

"The first time I saw that event in February 2024 in Vienna, I thought why is this not yet in India? This has a captive audience, is content friendly, is indoor, not dependent on weather and not challenging in the way of requiring permissions because it's in a private venue," he says.

"Besides, it has a much easier entry barrier," he says, adding without a moment's hesitation, "you could do it with some training."

Raj comes back to the "gym people," who are often social and sometime workout so they can post pictures. "Imagine, I'm giving them a studio. This is your studio. Walk in. Content will be created. Off you go. They didn't have a race of their own. Now, they have something to look up to, and with a community."

He had learnt from the Ironman experience that the community-running and fitness-embraces a new product before sponsors do. The first edition of Ironman 70.3 in Goa was sold out in 27 days, he says. "Brands (or sponsors) will come later, I thought. When I mean later, I didn't expect after three years (like Ironman because of the pandemic).

"So that was obviously a misreading in my head. It just took time here. The same thing happened with Hyrox."

The first edition of Hyrox (in India), in Mumbai in 2025, attracted 1,650 people. The September 2026 edition had 15,500 participants, ranging from the age of 16 to over 70. Athletes came from over 600 towns and cities, with 40 foreign entries over the four-day event. Each entry costs Rs.9,000, an indication of the amount of commitment the activity is attracting.

Raj is working on getting two more sporting or fitness properties to India, but declines to name them. He will add Chennai and Ahmedabad as Ironman 70.3 venues while the latter will also host the Ironman in 2028.

"India's coming around to the fact that you are reorganising your training schedules for months to train for a race, then maybe flying out on a Wednesday from Bengaluru to race on a Thursday in Mumbai," he says. "It's okay to fly on a Thursday/Friday, race on a Sunday, which happens for some marathons and Ironman events. Here, you are actually racing on a weekday (Hyrox). That makes me happy and realise that people are going the distance," he says, pun unintended.

Having now competed in about a dozen Hyrox events, he says it gives him a completely different high, compared to running or triathlon. "The intensity goes up and down, it exposed me to a lot of movements I was bad at. It's exposed me to areas in which I can get better."

Arun Janardhan (@iArunJ) is a Mumbai-based journalist who covers sports, business leaders and lifestyle.

data.title: Best of the Week | Jio's IPO frenzy: Can retail investors make a killing?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms opened its Rs.30,213-crore IPO on 21 October, with bidding closing on Friday. The offer, which could become India's largest-ever listing, values the digital and telecom giant at up to $107 billion. After securing strong institutional backing, Jio is counting on retail investors to help sustain demand and deliver a strong stock market debut.

The company allocated Rs.8,110 crore of shares to anchor investors, including BlackRock, Fidelity, Capital Group and sovereign wealth funds. Its Rs.10,500-crore retail portion has drawn active outreach from brokerages and financial institutions, even as the Nifty 50 struggles in a weak market.

Brokerages are also encouraging investors with inactive trading accounts to participate, while some financial institutions are offering loans to help fund applications. The push comes amid weak market sentiment, with the Nifty 50 down more than 10% this year.

Jio's appeal lies in its more than 500 million subscribers and leadership in wireless and fixed broadband. Yet its valuation warrants scrutiny. At the upper end of the price band, Jio is valued at about $107 billion, roughly 10% below rival Bharti Airtel. Airtel, however, generates more revenue per user, with June-quarter average revenue per user (ARPU) of Rs.264 against Jio's Rs.216, and has a higher earnings margin.

Analysts see potential in Jio's scale and digital services, but the company must turn its vast subscriber base into higher spending and stronger returns. Hyundai Motor India's heavily subscribed IPO, whose shares fell on debut, is a reminder that strong demand does not guarantee listing gains. Investors borrowing to apply also risk losses if the stock disappoints.

Can coal gasification cut India's import bill?

Jindal Steel's Odisha plant turns coal into synthetic gas at $7-8 per unit of energy, nearly half the cost of imported natural gas. India wants to scale up the technology to reduce dependence on overseas fuel and chemicals, backing projects with Rs.37,500 crore in incentives. But high upfront costs, ash-heavy coal and emissions remain hurdles to turning this ambitious bet into a viable business.

Tata Sons' filing adds to chairman reappointment row

Tata Sons' latest regulatory filing reappointing N. Chandrasekaran as executive chairman omits specific references to Articles 118 and 105, unlike previous filings. The omission matters because Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has challenged the reappointment, arguing that the board bypassed Article 118's requirement for a selection committee. Tata Sons maintains that the process was legally valid. The dispute centres on opposing votes by Tata Trusts nominees and a casting vote that cleared Chandrasekaran's five-year term, deepening tensions over governance at the group's holding company.

iPhone Duo scarcity adds Rs.50,000 bragging rights

Apple's Rs.2,99,900 iPhone Duo is so scarce that some Indian buyers are willing to pay up to Rs.50,000 extra to get one early. Only around 6,000 units are expected across India in its first week, pushing eager buyers towards grey-market sellers sourcing devices from Dubai and Singapore. Retailers say supplies are far below demand, with some receiving just a fraction of their orders. For buyers willing to spend nearly Rs.3 lakh on a phone, the premium is less about technology and more about the status of owning Apple's latest showpiece.

Why Musk is fighting for India's internet market

Elon Musk's public attacks on Indian telecom giants reflect a bigger business imperative: Starlink needs new markets to fuel SpaceX's growth. Its connectivity business generated 61% of SpaceX's revenue in 2025, while India remains largely off-limits despite regulatory approvals, with final clearance reportedly held up over security concerns. But entering India means confronting Jio and Airtel, which dominate the market and offer some of the world's cheapest data. Starlink must also slash prices to compete, even as rivals such as Amazon Leo expand their satellite networks.

India's cities are choking on dust

From Gurugram commuters to families battling respiratory illnesses, road and construction dust is making India's air pollution problem a year-round crisis. An IIT study found road dust levels exceeded WHO guidelines in 55% of cases, contributing to an estimated 10,000 deaths annually from PM2.5 pollution. Despite billions spent on dust management, cleaning often offers only temporary relief. Experts say cities need better monitoring, paved roads, stricter construction controls and targeted enforcement. The challenge is tackling dust at its source, before it settles on streets, rises into the air and enters our lungs.

AI's revenue squeeze leaves IT bosses divided

India's top IT firms disagree on whether AI-led revenue deflation, as automation reduces billable work, is nearing its end. HCLTech says the squeeze is still in its early stages, while TCS and Wipro see relief ahead. Tech Mahindra argues the threat is overstated. With legacy contracts shrinking and new AI revenue yet to fill the gap, uncertainty continues to weigh on investor sentiment.

India's growth faces a volatile world

Global growth is increasingly concentrated, with China, India and the US driving nearly 60% of the expansion. The West Asia war threatens growth, while AI investment provides an offset. India has sustained strong growth but remains vulnerable to geopolitical shocks, weak AI development and dependence on foreign capital. Boosting AI adoption, productivity and external financial stability will be crucial to sustaining its ambitions of becoming a developed economy.

Sebi plans review of IPO rules

Sebi plans to review regulations governing mainboard IPOs and further public offers, including eligibility criteria, promoter contributions, lock-in requirements and valuations. A sub-group under its Primary Markets Advisory Committee will examine the existing framework and suggest changes. The move comes amid broader scrutiny of public fundraising rules, including proposals to tighten listing requirements for small and medium enterprise IPOs.

Indian IT firms move upstream with AI consulting

India's top IT firms are expanding beyond software delivery to advise clients on AI model selection, costs and business transformation. TCS, HCLTech, Wipro and Tech Mahindra see falling AI costs opening new opportunities, following Accenture's lead.

The shift challenges a traditional business model built on labour arbitrage, as firms seek to influence technology decisions rather than simply execute them.

data.title: NIP Group Signs Bitcoin Miner Purchase To Add 4.47 Exahash Of Capacity
data.description:
TL;DR: NIP Group has agreed to purchase already deployed Bitcoin mining machines with about 4.47 EH/s of hash rate, subject to closing and share consideration.

Esports and digital infrastructure company NIP Group is moving deeper into Bitcoin mining through an agreement to acquire machines representing roughly 4.47 exahash per second of computing power.

The company said the equipment is already installed and operating at hosting sites. That reduces the need to construct new facilities for this particular tranche, but the deal remains subject to closing. The announcement is an agreement to acquire capacity, not confirmation that all of it has already been transferred into NIP Group's ownership.

A bigger mining operation paid for in shares

NIP Group plans to issue up to 247,091,740 Class A ordinary shares as consideration for the equipment. Share-based acquisitions can preserve cash, although the number and value of shares issued affect existing investors through potential dilution.

If the third tranche closes as planned, the company projects a combined mining capacity of approximately 13.85 EH/s across its acquisitions. That scale would make mining a substantial operation alongside the business's entertainment and infrastructure activities.

Management estimates the resulting capacity could produce around 195 Bitcoin per month at full deployment. That number is a model, not a guaranteed yield from machines. It depends on global network hash rate, mining difficulty, equipment uptime, power prices and the company's realized share of block rewards.

An increase in raw computing capacity has value only if the associated economics make sense. Higher Bitcoin prices can improve a miner's revenue in dollar terms, but competition often follows. More hardware joining the network can raise difficulty and reduce the coins each individual machine earns.

The AI infrastructure argument

NIP is positioning computing infrastructure as a bridge between digital entertainment, Bitcoin mining and potential high-performance or AI applications. Those markets share an appetite for electrical power, technical maintenance and large equipment installations, yet the hardware requirements are not interchangeable in every case.

Purpose-built Bitcoin mining chips do not turn into general AI accelerators just because both operate in data centers. What may transfer between the businesses is operational knowledge, access to power and the ability to manage large physical installations.

Investors should therefore distinguish three different propositions: purchasing mining equipment, generating Bitcoin from it and successfully diversifying into other computing services.

For now, the disclosed milestone is a signed purchase agreement with quantified hash rate and planned stock consideration. Closing terms, actual monthly production and energy economics will determine whether the expansion strengthens the business.

data.description:
Key points:
  • Jefferies said that despite management’s optimism that its backlog continues to grow faster than revenue, Bloom Energy did not provide a formal backlog update.
  • JPMorgan also lowered its price target on Bloom, cutting it to $292 from $314 while maintaining an ‘Overweight’ rating.
  • The firm attributed the reduction to lower trading multiples among Bloom Energy's peer group, despite noting that its execution “continues to impress.”

Bloom Energy Corp. (BE) shares suffered their steepest single-day decline in three months despite its third-quarter (Q3) results and fiscal year 2026 forecast surpassing Wall Street expectations.

According to TheFly, Jefferies lowered its price target on the fuel-cell power company, citing a lack of updates around delays tied to its largest opportunity with Oracle Corp. (ORCL).

Bloom Energy shares closed over 11% lower on Friday, falling about 0.3% further during the afterhours session.

Jefferies Flags Lack Of Updates On Oracle Opportunity

Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith lowered the firm's price target on Bloom Energy to $242 from $289 while maintaining a ‘Hold’ rating on the shares.

The target cut came after Bloom Energy raised its 2026 financial guidance for the third time this year.

Despite the company’s management remaining optimistic that its backlog continues to grow faster than revenue, Bloom Energy did not provide a formal backlog update, Dumoulin-Smith said in a note.

Bloom Energy did highlight recent customer wins, but the analyst said those wins were already well known.

JPMorgan also lowered its price target on Bloom, cutting it to $292 from $314 while maintaining an ‘Overweight’ rating. The firm attributed the reduction to lower trading multiples among Bloom Energy's peer group, despite noting that its execution “continues to impress.”

BTIG lowered its price target to $250 from $295 while maintaining a ‘Buy’ rating following the results. The firm pointed to a near-term margin drag as Bloom Energy ramps new production capacity and accommodates expedited customer timelines.

BTIG added that the cost of expanding manufacturing capacity is weighing on Bloom Energy’s margin outlook.

Bloom Energy Reports Record Q3 Revenue

Bloom Energy reported record third-quarter revenue of $1.24 billion on Thursday, up 138.1% year over year, with product revenue rising 179.4% to $1.07 billion.

Gross margin increased to 33.8% from 29.2% a year earlier, while operating income rose to $225.4 million from $7.8 million. Its adjusted earnings per share (EPS) came in at $0.94, compared with 15 cents a year earlier.

Bloom Energy also raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $4.4 billion-$4.6 billion, representing 122% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. The company now expects full-year adjusted EPS of $3.1-$3.4.

Wall Street expected Bloom Energy to report adjusted EPS of $0.68 on revenue of $1.07 billion, according to Fiscal.ai data.

What Retail Investors Think About BE Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Bloom Energy trended in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

BE stock is up 122% year-to-date and 91% over the past 12 months. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 11% over the past 12 months, while the Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) is up 10%.
